To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the miR‐143 and miR‐145 microRNA genes are essential for stretch-induced contractile differentiation of vascular smooth muscle.
the microRNA cluster miR‐143 and miR‐145 is essential for stretch‐dependent differentiation of vascular smooth muscle, and for maintaining the contractility of the portal vein in vivo.

the miR‐143‐145 cluster is essential for stretch‐mediated contractile differentiation of vascular smooth muscle, as demonstrated by a reduction in spontaneous activity and stretch‐mediated differentiation in knockout mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of the microRNA‐143/145 cluster in the regulation of vascular smooth muscle phenotype and stretch‐inducible differentiation.
the importance of the miR‐143 and miR‐145 microRNA cluster in the differentiation of vascular smooth muscle.
the role of miR‐145 in the differentiation and contractile properties of vascular smooth muscle in response to stretch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

miR‐143 and miR‐145 are essential for stretch induced differentiation of vascular smooth muscle, and the absence of this microRNA cluster results in a significant reduction in the expression of the contractile proteins, α‐actin, calponin, and caldesmon.

the smooth muscle‐expressed microRNA cluster, miR‐143 and miR‐145, plays an important role in maintaining the contractile smooth muscle phenotype and is required for stretch‐inducible differentiation of vascular smooth muscle.
microRNAs, and miR‐143 in particular, play an important role in the stretch‐induced regulation of the contractile phenotype in vascular smooth muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

miR‐143‐5p and miR‐145‐5p are important for stretch‐inducible expression of the L‐type calcium channels Cav1.2 and Cav1.3, as well as the contractile proteins SM22α and SM α‐actin in vascular smooth muscle cells.
the miR‐143‐145 cluster is essential for the differentiation of the smooth muscle cell phenotype and the regulation of L‐Ca2+ channel expression.
microRNAs play important roles in stretch‐induced vascular differentiation, and the miR‐143‐145 microRNA cluster plays an important role in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

miR‐143 and miR‐145 are important for stretch‐inducible differentiation of vascular smooth muscle and for maintaining the contractility of the portal vein, and that this effect is likely due to regulation of the expression of smooth muscle‐specific contractile proteins.
microRNAs, and in particular the miR‐143‐145 cluster, are essential for maintaining the smooth muscle contractile phenotype in the absence of stretch.
miR‐143 is essential for maintaining a differentiated state of vascular smooth muscle.
